raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

With `--enable-torch-compile`, MiniMax-H3 serves slower than in eager. On 2xGB300, t2va 5 s, Ulysses 2, compile is 61.5 s against 57.7 s eager. vLLM-Omni's default (compiled) run is 60.9 s.

The attention section gates its fast paths on `not torch.compiler.is_compiling()`, so a compiled DiT loses all of them:

- the fused qk-norm + RoPE;
- the head-group pipelined Ulysses exchange over the copy engine;
- the IPC all-to-all.

Those paths cannot be traced. The traceable fallback that compile takes instead (unfused norm and RoPE, a sequential exchange) costs more than inductor saves on the rest of the block.

## Modifications

- The section from the per-head q/k norm through the attention output (before `out_proj`) moves into `MiniMaxH3Attention._attend`.
- Eager calls `_attend` as before. Under compile, `forward` calls `_attend_eager = torch.compiler.disable(_attend)`, so that section runs exactly the eager fast paths, and inductor compiles the QKV/out projections, MLP, AdaLN and norms around it.
- The `is_compiling()` gate inside the section goes away, since compile no longer traces it.

Eager behavior is unchanged: the same calls in the same order.

## Accuracy Tests

Eager is unchanged (same code path). Under compile, the attention section now runs the same fused kernels as eager, instead of the unfused fallback.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

2xGB300, MiniMax-H3 t2va 5 s, Ulysses 2, served. Base: main 3831e7e09, the then-open GB300 fixes and #43602; compile arms use `--offload-during-compile false`. Each cell is the median of 2 requests after warmup, every arm on a fresh server; the second compile round runs the arms in the opposite order.

| | before | this PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| eager | 57.667 s | 57.554 s (unchanged) |
| torch.compile, round 1 | 61.378 s | **58.712 s (−4.3%)** |
| torch.compile, round 2 | 61.590 s | **58.609 s (−4.8%)** |

vLLM-Omni's default (compiled) run is 60.95 s on the same box. Compile is still slightly behind eager for H3, but it no longer loses its fast attention paths.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests: `test_minimax_h3_dit_contract.py`. `forward` dispatches to `_attend` in eager and to `_attend_eager` under compile, and `_attend_eager` is hidden from Dynamo. On GB300 (main 9336681 + this PR), with `test_minimax_h3_denoise_loop.py` and `test_hybrid_window_h3_attention.py`: 45 passed.
- [ ] Update documentation: N/A.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance.

+        # The fused qk-norm/RoPE, pipelined Ulysses exchange and attention kernels
+        # are untraceable, and the traceable fallback is slower than eager, so a
+        # compiled DiT runs this section eager and compiles around it.
+        attend = self._attend_eager if torch.compiler.is_compiling() else self._attend

@@ -850,3 +850,35 @@ def test_cuda_ulysses_qkv_pack_is_bit_exact():

     torch.testing.assert_close(actual, expected, rtol=0, atol=0)
+

+@pytest.mark.parametrize("compiling", [False, True])
+def test_compiled_attention_runs_its_fused_section_eager(compiling):
+    _ensure_single_process_parallel_runtime()
+    arch = MiniMaxH3DiTArchConfig()
+    with torch.device("meta"):
+        attention = MiniMaxH3Attention(arch, None, prefix="blocks.0.attn")
+    tokens = 4
+    out = torch.empty(tokens, attention.local_inner_dim, device="meta")
+
+    with (
+        patch.object(torch.compiler, "is_compiling", return_value=compiling),
+        patch.object(MiniMaxH3Attention, "_attend", return_value=out) as attend,
+        patch.object(
+            MiniMaxH3Attention, "_attend_eager", return_value=out
+        ) as attend_eager,
+    ):
+        result = attention(
+            torch.empty(tokens, arch.hidden_size, device="meta"),
+            rope_cache=None,
+            cu_seqlens=torch.empty(2, dtype=torch.int32, device="meta"),
+            max_seqlen=tokens,
+        )
+
+    assert result.shape == (tokens, arch.hidden_size)
+    assert (attend_eager if compiling else attend).call_count == 1
+    assert (attend if compiling else attend_eager).call_count == 0
+
+
+def test_eager_attention_section_is_hidden_from_dynamo():
+    assert MiniMaxH3Attention._attend_eager._torchdynamo_disable
